name: The applicant organization's sponsored programmes office
what: [NIH](#term:nih)'s help and planning pages send applicants first to their own organization's [office of sponsored research](#term:sponsored-programs-office), which explains the process and roles and sets up system accounts [146](#cite:146) [119](#cite:119).

name: NIH programme official (programme officer)
what: Institute staff who know a scientific area and the institute's priorities; they can assess fit, explain how policy applies and help interpret review feedback, and they do not edit applications or discuss review details [92](#cite:92) [120](#cite:120).

name: NIH Matchmaker (in RePORTER)
what: A tool that takes an abstract or other scientific text and returns similar funded projects, the institutes that fund them and the programme officials attached [120](#cite:120) [92](#cite:92).

name: Explore NIH Opportunities
what: [NIH](#term:nih)'s search tool over [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) with NIH-specific filters, sorting and advanced search [93](#cite:93) [105](#cite:105).

name: ICO Funding Policies and Considerations pages
what: One page per institute, center or office stating the factors it weighs in funding decisions and any across-the-board budget policies, built on the NIH-wide framework [67](#cite:67) [123](#cite:123).

variants.what: Technical help with ASSIST, [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) and Internet Assisted Review [146](#cite:146).
Helps with application submission through eRA Commons for [AHRQ](#term:ahrq) and FDA notices; telephone 301-402-7469 or 866-504-9552 [507](#cite:507) [564](#cite:564).

name: eRA Service Desk
what: Help with eRA Commons, ASSIST, registration, errors and warnings, application status, Internet Assisted Review and post-award modules such as the [RPPR](#term:rppr) [1912](#cite:1912). Hours are Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET, closed on federal holidays; telephone 1-866-504-9552 or 301-402-7469; web tickets at https://public.era.nih.gov/submithelp/ [1912](#cite:1912). The desk asks those within two days of a deadline to call [1912](#cite:1912).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to and recipients of [NIH](#term:nih) and the other agencies that use eRA, [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) among them [1912](#cite:1912) [548](#cite:548).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1912](#cite:1912).

name: NSF programme officers
what: Each funding opportunity lists one or more [programme officers](#term:program-officer); BIO tells applicants to contact the programme director to ask whether a programme fits the research [158](#cite:158) [186](#cite:186).

name: NSF webinars and office hours
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) staff hold webinars and office hours on funding opportunities; CMMI scheduled a webinar on its 2026 [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) for September 14, 2026 [158](#cite:158) [198](#cite:198).

variants.what: System support is at 1-800-381-1532 or rgov@nsf.gov [165](#cite:165).

name: NSF IT Service Desk (Research.gov)
what: System support for [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) at 1-800-381-1532 or rgov@nsf.gov, 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday to Friday except federal holidays [1972](#cite:1972).
who_it_is_for: Research.gov users, including those setting up multifactor sign-in [1972](#cite:1972).
cost: No charge is stated in the document read [1972](#cite:1972).

name: NSF Policy Office
what: Questions on proposal and award policy go to policy@nsf.gov [165](#cite:165) [248](#cite:248).

name: Help placing an interdisciplinary proposal
what: For research with no obvious programme home [NSF](#term:nsf) points to its interdisciplinary-research page [158](#cite:158).

name: PAMS help desk (DOE Office of Science)
what: Telephone (855) 818-1846 (toll-free) or (301) 903-9610; sc.pams-helpdesk@science.doe.gov [282](#cite:282).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to and awardees of the [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) [282](#cite:282).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [282](#cite:282).

variants.what: Telephone (301) 682-5507, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET; help@[eBRAP](#term:ebrap).org [358](#cite:358).

name: eBRAP help desk (CDMRP)
what: Telephone (301) 682-5507; help@eBRAP.org; Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, except holidays [358](#cite:358). The site also has a user guide, questions and answers, and a page of commonly made mistakes [358](#cite:358).
who_it_is_for: [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) applicants and their organisations [358](#cite:358).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [358](#cite:358).

name: NSPIRES Help Desk (NASA)
what: Telephone (202) 479-9376, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern; nspires-help@nasaprs.com [1947](#cite:1947) [377](#cite:377).
who_it_is_for: NASA proposers and their organisations [1947](#cite:1947).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1947](#cite:1947).

name: NASA SMD programme officers list
what: A directory of contacts by division and programme element, last updated September 18, 2026 [390](#cite:390).

name: NASA new PI resources and review-panel volunteering
what: A page for first-time proposers, with a route to serve on review panels, which NASA says is a way to learn what it values in proposals [388](#cite:388) [391](#cite:391).

name: DARPAConnect
what: [DARPA](#term:darpa)'s resource offering curriculum, proposal support, mentoring and coaching [345](#cite:345).

variants.what: Telephone 800-518-4726 (domestic) or 606-545-5035 (international); support@[grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), as listed by ONR [336](#cite:336).
Grants.gov support is at support@grants.gov or 1-800-518-4726 [644](#cite:644) [665](#cite:665).

name: Grants.gov Applicant Support and training
what: Grants.gov Applicant Support is available 24/7 except federal holidays, at 1-800-518-4726 or support@grants.gov [1917](#cite:1917) [1965](#cite:1965). The support page also offers a chatbot, a Frequently Asked Questions portal, the [Grants](#term:grant) Learning Center, Online Help and Applicant Training [1917](#cite:1917). Agencies tell applicants to keep the case number as evidence of a technical problem [548](#cite:548) [1928](#cite:1928).
who_it_is_for: Organisations and individuals registering or applying through Grants.gov [1917](#cite:1917).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1917](#cite:1917).

name: Office of Science grants and contracts support
what: Contact address sc.grantsandcontracts@doe.gov [284](#cite:284).

name: NIFA application help
what: General questions about the [NIFA](#term:nifa) application process go to GrantApplicationQuestions@usda.gov; [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) questions go to Support@Grants.gov [421](#cite:421).

name: AFRI notice resources page
what: [NIFA](#term:nifa) gathers the AFRI [grant](#term:grant) types, project types, review criteria, new-investigator decision tree, strengthening-eligibility flow chart and [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) instructions on one page, with tables of the most and least successful institutions [420](#cite:420).

name: State Water Resources Research Institute directors
what: The institute director or designee submits water resources applications for investigators in the state; USGS publishes a directory of the institutes [485](#cite:485) [484](#cite:484).

name: State Sea Grant programmes
what: Each of the 34 Sea [Grant](#term:grant) programmes lists its own funding opportunities and is the first contact for a researcher in its state [437](#cite:437).

name: OJP Response Center
what: Takes questions about open Office of Justice Programs notices, including NIJ and BJS notices, by telephone at 800-851-3420 [602](#cite:602).

name: PCORI applicant town halls and helpdesk
what: [PCORI](#term:pcori) holds an applicant town hall for each funding announcement and answers questions at pfa@pcori.org [593](#cite:593) [591](#cite:591).

name: NIDILRR informational calls
what: [NIDILRR](#term:acl) holds an informational call for some notices before the [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) date and gives a general mailbox, nidilrr-mailbox@acl.hhs.gov [579](#cite:579) [576](#cite:576).

name: NIOSH extramural programme contact form
what: Routes a question to the [NIOSH](#term:cdc) team for finance, programme or review matters; Scientific Review Officers give prospective applicants information on the review process [553](#cite:553).

name: IES virtual office hours
what: Drop-in Zoom or phone sessions with [programme officers](#term:program-officer) for each open competition, 1:00-4:00 PM ET on listed dates; sessions are not recorded [724](#cite:724).

name: NEH evaluator ratings and comments on request
what: Any [NEH](#term:neh) applicant can ask for the evaluators' ratings and written comments on its application; evaluators' names are not given [638](#cite:638).

name: NEH Office of Grant Management
what: Answers administrative and cost questions at grantmanagement@neh.gov or 202-606-8494; programme questions go to the division named in the notice [644](#cite:644).

name: IMLS programme staff
what: [IMLS](#term:imls) gives a mailbox for library programmes (imls-librarygrants@imls.gov) and a named contact with a booking calendar for National Leadership [Grants](#term:grant) for Museums [676](#cite:676) [680](#cite:680).

name: NHPRC optional draft review
what: NHPRC announcements set an optional draft deadline ahead of the final deadline (for example August 15, 2025 before November 5, 2025), and staff directors are listed by programme line [698](#cite:698) [696](#cite:696) [725](#cite:725).

name: NIH Division of Biomedical Research Workforce
what: The office in [NIH](#term:nih)'s Office of Extramural Research named as the contact for the August 2026 changes to [K awards](#term:k-award); its address is dbrw@nih.gov [742](#cite:742).

name: NIH institute-by-institute considerations and contacts for fellowships and career awards
what: [NIH](#term:nih) keeps one page for individual fellowships and one for individual [career development awards](#term:k-award) that set out, institute by institute, which codes are funded, the extra limits and support levels each sets, and staff contacts [804](#cite:804) [805](#cite:805). A third page does the same for institutional [training grants](#term:t32) [813](#cite:813).

name: Institute LRP scientific liaisons and programme officers
what: [Loan repayment](#term:loan-repayment) applicants are encouraged to contact the awarding institute's LRP scientific liaison; [NIH](#term:nih) lists LRP [programme officers](#term:program-officer) on its extramural LRP pages [763](#cite:763) [762](#cite:762).

name: NIH Research Training and Career Development pages
what: [NIH](#term:nih)'s landing page sorts its training and career programmes into those an individual applies for (fellowships, individual career development) and those an institution applies for (institutional training, research education, institutional career development); the old address researchtraining.nih.gov redirects to it [727](#cite:727). The policy statement's section on individual fellowships is reached through subsection pages, the heading page being blank [768](#cite:768).

name: GRFP help (grfp@nsf.gov and the GRF Operations Center)
what: [GRFP](#term:grfp) questions go to grfp@nsf.gov [817](#cite:817). Applicants and reference writers who need accessibility accommodation are asked to tell the GRF Operations Center at least three weeks before the deadline [818](#cite:818).

name: CAREER programme contact
what: The CAREER opportunity page gives one contact for the programme, nsf-ccc@nsf.gov, (703) 292-5111, and links a question-and-answer document, [NSF](#term:nsf) 22-100 [814](#cite:814) [816](#cite:816).

name: NSF directory of REU Sites
what: Students look for an REU Site in [NSF](#term:nsf)'s directory and apply to the Site itself, not to NSF [869](#cite:869) [829](#cite:829).

name: NSF funding pages by career stage
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) keeps landing pages for undergraduates, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers and early-career researchers that list opportunities with headline amounts [835](#cite:835) [834](#cite:834) [833](#cite:833) [251](#cite:251). On 2026-10-04 these pages still listed programmes whose own pages were archived, so the status of a programme is the one shown on its own page [251](#cite:251) [843](#cite:843) [845](#cite:845) [838](#cite:838).

name: SCGSR applicant workshops and office hours
what: For the open SCGSR [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) the programme listed workshops on September 3, 2026 and October 1, 2026, and weekly office hours from September 4, 2026 [892](#cite:892).

name: Army Research Office technical point of contact
what: The ARL announcement strongly recommends a discussion with the cognizant ARO technical point of contact before an Early Career Program proposal is submitted [341](#cite:341).

name: NDSEG programme office
what: The NDSEG application site gives NDSEG.PMO@sysplus.com and (301) 948-4232 as the programme contact [913](#cite:913).

name: National Sea Grant Office fellowships contact
what: Sea [Grant](#term:grant) gives oar.sg.fellows@noaa.gov for fellowship questions, and directs students to the Sea Grant programme in their state [436](#cite:436) [966](#cite:966).

name: NASA ECIP-ES information sessions and programme contacts
what: For the ROSES-2025 round NASA held two virtual information sessions, on May 14 and May 26, 2026, and named two programme contacts [952](#cite:952).

name: C&GC fellowship question-and-answer session
what: The fellowship administrator held a question-and-answer session for applicants on September 3, 2026 [971](#cite:971).

name: Campus Fulbright Program Adviser
what: A student enrolled at a U.S. college or university applies to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program through that institution and is told to find the Fulbright Program Adviser on campus [1023](#cite:1023).

name: NEH Division of Research programme mailboxes
what: [NEH](#term:neh) gives a mailbox for each individual award: fellowships@neh.gov, publicscholar@neh.gov and FacultyAwards@neh.gov, with the Division of Research telephone 202-606-8200 [986](#cite:986) [1003](#cite:1003) [1004](#cite:1004).

name: HRSA primary care NRSA mailbox
what: The [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) listing for HRSA-26-035 gives HRSANRSA@hrsa.gov as the programme contact [1027](#cite:1027).

name: SAMHSA notice contacts (programme, budget, review)
what: Each [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) notice names three contacts, one in the programme centre for programme and eligibility questions, the Division of [Grants](#term:grant) Management for budget questions, and the Division of Grant Review for review and application status [1112](#cite:1112).

name: HRSA Bureau of Primary Health Care funding contact
what: Health Center Program applicants are directed to bphcfunding@hrsa.gov and 301-594-4300; look-alike applicants to a contact form and 877-464-4772 [1149](#cite:1149) [1216](#cite:1216).

name: Technical assistance for rural community programme grantees
what: The Federal Office of Rural Health Policy states that technical assistance for its community-based programmes is provided by the Georgia Health Policy Center (ruralhealthlink.org) [1161](#cite:1161).

name: HRSA awarded grants search
what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s [grants](#term:grant) page links a tool for searching HRSA-awarded grants [1145](#cite:1145).

name: Local Continuum of Care and its Collaborative Applicant
what: The local body through which a homeless-services project applies for HUD [Continuum of Care](#term:continuum-of-care) funds; it runs the local competition and files the consolidated application [1283](#cite:1283).

name: State Administrative Agency (Nonprofit Security Grant Program)
what: The state agency that takes non-profits' NSGP applications, scores them and applies to FEMA [1320](#cite:1320).

name: State VOCA administrator
what: The state agency that makes Victims of Crime Act [subawards](#term:subaward) to local service providers; OVC lists contacts on its State Support map [1279](#cite:1279).

name: Find Your CAA (Community Action Agency locator)
what: [ACF](#term:acf)'s tool for finding the local Community Action Agency that delivers CSBG-funded services [1239](#cite:1239).

name: Office of Head Start application help line
what: The contact for questions about Head Start applications - OHSgrants@koniag-gs.com or 888-242-0684 [1225](#cite:1225).

name: OVW Resources for Applicants and Application Companion Guide
what: OVW's sample documents (budget narrative, memorandum of understanding, certification letters) and its yearly companion guide [1349](#cite:1349) [1270](#cite:1270).

name: American Job Center
what: The local point of delivery for WIOA services; ETA gives 1-877-US-2JOBS for finding one [1304](#cite:1304).

name: State service commission (AmeriCorps)
what: The body through which a State receives [AmeriCorps](#term:americorps) State and National formula and state-competitive funds and makes [subgrants](#term:subaward) [1377](#cite:1377).

name: State or jurisdictional arts agency
what: One of 56 agencies that receive [NEA](#term:nea) Partnership Agreement [grants](#term:grant) and make their own grants to arts organisations in the state [1359](#cite:1359) [1360](#cite:1360).

name: State or jurisdictional humanities council
what: One of 56 councils funded by [NEH](#term:neh) that run and sponsor local humanities programmes; NEH offers a contact list [1366](#cite:1366).

name: State Library Administrative Agency
what: The state agency that receives [IMLS](#term:imls) [Grants](#term:grant) to States and makes [subawards](#term:subaward) to libraries [1372](#cite:1372).

name: State 21st Century Community Learning Centers coordinator
what: The contact at each state educational agency for the state's 21st CCLC competition, listed on the Department of Education's programme page [1399](#cite:1399).

name: USDA Rural Development state office
what: The office an applicant contacts before applying for Community Facilities or RCDI money [1410](#cite:1410) [1411](#cite:1411).

name: ARC state program manager
what: The state official with whom an ARC Area Development application begins; deadlines are set by the state [1445](#cite:1445).

name: Local Development District (Delta Regional Authority)
what: The local body DRA tells SEDAP applicants to contact for help with an application [1447](#cite:1447).

name: EDA economic development representative
what: The regional office contact for applicants to EDA [1431](#cite:1431).

name: ORIP S10 office hours
what: ORIP holds [S10](#term:s10) office hours on Wednesdays from 2 to 3 pm Eastern [1534](#cite:1534).

name: NSF EPSCoR office hours and programme contact
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) schedules office hours for its [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) (E-CORE office hours were listed for July 28, July 31, August 5 and August 7, 2026) and answers questions at nsfepscor@nsf.gov [866](#cite:866).

name: NSF MRI programme contact
what: Questions about MRI go to mri@nsf.gov or 703-292-8040 [1515](#cite:1515).

name: NASA EPSCoR jurisdiction directors
what: NASA publishes a list of [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) directors, one for each participating jurisdiction [1570](#cite:1570).

name: NIGMS Division for Research Capacity Building staff contacts
what: The IDeA page links the division's staff contacts by programme area [1543](#cite:1543).

name: DURIP pre-proposal inquiries
what: Questions on the FY 2027 DURIP announcement are due October 16, 2026 [1563](#cite:1563).

name: Department of Education eligibility designation technical assistance
what: The eligibility page names a technical assistance contact (Nemeka Mason-Clercin, nemeka.mason@ed.gov, 202-987-1340) and points to a recorded webinar under GEA Resources at hepis.ed.gov [1595](#cite:1595).

name: NIFA 1890 institutions mailbox
what: [NIFA](#term:nifa) gives 1890@usda.gov as the mailbox for requests from 1890 institutions about Evans-Allen funds [1635](#cite:1635).

name: NASA MSI Exchange
what: NASA's [MSI](#term:minority-serving-institution) Exchange site holds the NASA MSI List used to check eligibility for MUREP [1629](#cite:1629).

name: NSF TCUP and HBCU programme mailboxes
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) gives tcup@nsf.gov for the [Tribal Colleges](#term:tribal-college) and Universities Program, HBCU_UP@nsf.gov for HBCU-UP and EIR@nsf.gov for HBCU-EiR [1613](#cite:1613) [1611](#cite:1611) [1610](#cite:1610).

name: A Member's or Senator's office (appropriations requests)
what: The only door into the [earmark](#term:community-project-funding) process: each House Member's and each Senator's office takes project requests on its own form and deadline, ahead of the committee deadlines, and must post what it submits [1667](#cite:1667) [1674](#cite:1674). One Senator's office guide said its deadline would be announced once the subcommittees announced theirs [1684](#cite:1684).

name: HUD Community Planning and Development field office and regional environmental officer
what: HUD's field offices administer earmarked Economic Development Initiative [grants](#term:grant), and regional environmental officers help grantees with the environmental review [1685](#cite:1685).

name: HRSA CDS Program mailbox and training page
what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa) answers named recipients at cdsprogram@hrsa.gov (CDSProgram2026@hrsa.gov for FY 2026) and posts webinars, pre-award forms and post-award guidance on its [Community Project Funding](#term:community-project-funding) page [1708](#cite:1708) [1687](#cite:1687).

name: National Park Service STLPG grants mailbox
what: STLPG@nps.gov is the contact on each Historic Preservation Fund competitive notice [1696](#cite:1696) [1701](#cite:1701).

name: AmeriCorps region office
what: The region office gives a prospective VISTA sponsor technical assistance during the application [1723](#cite:1723).

name: HUD capacity building and technical assistance mailboxes
what: HUD's notices give capacitybuilding@hud.gov for Section 4 and Rural Capacity Building, communitycompass@hud.gov for Community Compass and distressedcities@hud.gov for Distressed Cities Technical Assistance [1712](#cite:1712) [1714](#cite:1714) [1715](#cite:1715) [1716](#cite:1716).

name: HHS Cost Allocation Services (indirect cost rate negotiation)
what: The [HHS](#term:hhs) office that negotiates [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates for colleges and universities, non-profit organisations, hospitals and state and local governments [1860](#cite:1860). Proposals go through its Indirect Cost Allocation System portal; questions go to cas_admin@psc.hhs.gov and portal support to support_icas@psc.hhs.gov [1860](#cite:1860).
who_it_is_for: Organisations for which HHS is the [cognizant agency for indirect costs](#term:cognizant-agency) [1860](#cite:1860) [1849](#cite:1849).
cost: No fee is stated on the page [1860](#cite:1860).

name: ONR Indirect Cost Branch
what: The Office of Naval Research branch that negotiates [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates for the domestic colleges, universities and non-profit entities for which ONR has rate cognizance [1861](#cite:1861). Its page carries proposal guides for universities (long form, short form, rate extensions) and for non-profits (initial, [renewal](#term:renewal), and under $10M a year in direct federal funding); the Director's number is 571-368-6804 [1861](#cite:1861).
who_it_is_for: Universities and non-profits whose [cognizant agency](#term:cognizant-agency) is the Department of Defense [1861](#cite:1861) [1849](#cite:1849).
cost: No fee is stated on the page [1861](#cite:1861).

name: NSF Cost Analysis and Pre-Award Branch
what: The [NSF](#term:nsf) branch that negotiates [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates for about 100 organisations for which NSF is the [cognizant agency](#term:cognizant-agency); its page explains the [de minimis](#term:de-minimis-rate) option and the six-month deadline for yearly proposals [163](#cite:163).
who_it_is_for: Organisations for which NSF is the cognizant agency, and NSF applicants with no [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [163](#cite:163).
cost: No fee is stated on the page [163](#cite:163).

name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse and its helpdesk
what: The GSA site where [single audits](#term:single-audit) are submitted and where anyone may search filed audits; it has a helpdesk and a list of [cognizant agency](#term:cognizant-agency) contacts [1881](#cite:1881). Sign-in is through [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) [1881](#cite:1881).
who_it_is_for: Organisations that must file a single audit, their auditors, and [pass-through entities](#term:pass-through-entity) checking a [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) [1881](#cite:1881) [1846](#cite:1846).
cost: No fee is stated on the page [1881](#cite:1881).

name: Grants.gov grant terminology glossary
what: A glossary of the terms federal funding notices use, including discretionary, mandatory and [formula grants](#term:formula-grant), [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), [continuation](#term:continuation) [grant](#term:grant) and [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) [1880](#cite:1880).
who_it_is_for: Anyone reading a first federal funding notice [1880](#cite:1880).
cost: Free public web page [1880](#cite:1880).

name: OMB Office of Federal Financial Management grants mailbox
what: The contact [OMB](#term:omb) gives in the [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) for questions about the government-wide [grants](#term:grant) rules: MBX.OMB.Grants@OMB.eop.gov [1458](#cite:1458). CFO.gov and COFFA.gov hold the 2024 redline, implementation memorandum and reference guides for the [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) [1882](#cite:1882).
who_it_is_for: Research offices and non-profit finance staff with questions about 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) [1458](#cite:1458).

name: HHS Departmental Appeals Board (grant disputes)
what: The board that hears appeals of certain final written decisions in [HHS](#term:hhs) [discretionary grant](#term:discretionary-grant) programmes: disallowances, [terminations](#term:termination) for failure to comply with the terms of an award, denials of [noncompeting continuation](#term:continuation) for failure to comply, and voidings [1888](#cite:1888). A 30-day period applies to the notice of appeal [1888](#cite:1888).
who_it_is_for: Recipients of HHS discretionary grants that receive one of the listed decisions [1888](#cite:1888).
cost: No fee is stated in the appendix read [1888](#cite:1888).

name: Federal Service Desk (SAM.gov help)
what: GSA's help desk for [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration, [renewal](#term:renewal), entity validation and [subaward](#term:subaward) reporting [619](#cite:619) [1904](#cite:1904). DOJ gives its hours as Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET, except federal holidays, and [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) gives its telephone number as 866-606-8220, with a chat [619](#cite:619) [1965](#cite:1965). GSA tells entities to answer emails from fsdsupport@gsa.gov [1968](#cite:1968).
who_it_is_for: Any organisation registering or renewing in SAM.gov, or reporting subawards there [1904](#cite:1904).
cost: No charge is stated; SAM.gov itself is free to use [1898](#cite:1898).

name: Simpler.Grants.gov feedback and release notes
what: The [Simpler.Grants.gov](#term:simpler-grants) team takes feedback at simpler@[grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and publishes a roadmap and dated release notes; technical support remains with Grants.gov at support@grants.gov or 1-800-518-4726 [1967](#cite:1967) [1919](#cite:1919) [1920](#cite:1920).
who_it_is_for: Anyone using the new search or the application pilot [1967](#cite:1967).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1967](#cite:1967).

name: JustGrants Service Desk and OVW JustGrants support
what: For the COPS Office and [OJP](#term:office-of-justice-programs): 833-872-5175, Monday to Friday 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. ET and Saturday, Sunday and federal holidays 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET [1924](#cite:1924). For OVW: 866-655-4482, Monday to Friday 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET [1924](#cite:1924). OJP asks applicants to keep service desk tracking numbers, which a request to submit late must include [619](#cite:619).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to and recipients of DOJ [grant](#term:grant) programmes [1924](#cite:1924).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1924](#cite:1924).

name: HRSA Contact Center
what: Telephone 1-877-464-4772 (TTY 877-897-9910), Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., except federal holidays; it handles [Electronic Handbooks](#term:hrsa-ehbs) accounts [1925](#cite:1925) [1927](#cite:1927). [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) and ID.me problems go to those services' own help pages [1926](#cite:1926).
who_it_is_for: [HRSA](#term:hrsa) applicants and grantees [1925](#cite:1925).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1925](#cite:1925).

name: GrantSolutions Help Desk
what: [ACF](#term:acf) directs recipients to the [GrantSolutions](#term:grantsolutions) Help Desk, at help@grantsolutions.gov, or to the assigned [Grants Management Specialist](#term:grants-management-officer) [1961](#cite:1961). [CDC](#term:cdc) keeps its own support and contacts page for GrantSolutions [1962](#cite:1962).
who_it_is_for: Recipients of awards managed in GrantSolutions [1961](#cite:1961).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1961](#cite:1961).

name: Department of Education G6 help desk (OBSS)
what: The Office of Business Support Services Helpdesk at 202-401-6238 or toll free 888-336-8930 [1964](#cite:1964) [1963](#cite:1963).
who_it_is_for: Department of Education grantees using [G6](#term:ed-g6) [1964](#cite:1964).
cost: No charge is stated in the documents read [1964](#cite:1964).

name: ezFedGrants help (USDA)
what: General questions go to ezFedGrants-cfo@usda.gov; the page also lists a contact address for each agency that uses the system [1929](#cite:1929).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to and recipients of USDA agencies that use [ezFedGrants](#term:ezfedgrants) [1929](#cite:1929).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1929](#cite:1929).

name: IMLS eGMS Reach help desk and job aids
what: Reach-HelpDesk@imls.gov for system questions and grantsadmin@imls.gov, with the award number in the subject line, for award questions [1960](#cite:1960) [1933](#cite:1933). [IMLS](#term:imls) publishes five job aids: using [Login.gov](#term:login-gov), navigating the system, and submitting a change request, a payment request and a report [1960](#cite:1960).
who_it_is_for: IMLS awardees and peer reviewers [1960](#cite:1960).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1960](#cite:1960).

name: FEMA GO Help Desk
what: Telephone 877-585-3242; FEMAGO@fema.dhs.gov [1958](#cite:1958). FEMA's FAQ gives the hours as 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday to Friday, and its 2021 account guide gives 8 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET [1958](#cite:1958) [1959](#cite:1959).
who_it_is_for: Users of [FEMA GO](#term:fema-go) [1958](#cite:1958).
cost: No charge is stated in the documents read [1958](#cite:1958).

name: e-snaps technical help and HUD Exchange Ask A Question
what: Technical, account and navigation questions go to [e-snaps](#term:e-snaps)@hud.gov; policy questions go to the HUD Exchange Ask A Question portal, choosing [CoC](#term:continuum-of-care) Program [1935](#cite:1935).
who_it_is_for: Collaborative Applicants and project applicants in the Continuum of Care Program [1935](#cite:1935).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1935](#cite:1935).

name: Payment Management System Help Desk
what: Telephone 1-877-614-5533; PMSSupport@psc.hhs.gov; Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET, except federal holidays; a self-service portal is also offered [1975](#cite:1975). Sign-on problems go to XMSHelp@hhs.gov [1974](#cite:1974).
who_it_is_for: Recipients that draw funds or file financial reports in [PMS](#term:payment-management-system) [1975](#cite:1975).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1975](#cite:1975).

name: ASAP help desk (Treasury)
what: Telephone 816-414-2145; asaphelpdesk@fiscal.treasury.gov; Monday to Friday except federal holidays, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Eastern [1956](#cite:1956). [NIFA](#term:nifa) lists an [ASAP](#term:asap-payments) customer service number at the Kansas City Financial Center, (855) 868-0151, and DOJ lists 800-458-0786 for ASAP payment questions [1931](#cite:1931) [1924](#cite:1924).
who_it_is_for: Recipient organisations enrolled in ASAP [1956](#cite:1956).
cost: ASAP is free for recipient organisations [1937](#cite:1937).

name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse helpdesk and submission guide
what: The [FAC](#term:federal-audit-clearinghouse) helpdesk is at support.fac.gov; the site also has an illustrated submission guide, the SF-SAC workbooks with instructions, and a page on changing certifying officials and editors [1881](#cite:1881).
who_it_is_for: Auditees and auditors submitting a [single audit](#term:single-audit) [1938](#cite:1938).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1881](#cite:1881).

name: SciENcv help (NCBI Support Center)
what: Technical help with [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) comes from the NCBI Support Center at the National Library of Medicine [1943](#cite:1943). NASA sends questions about its own forms to hq-dlgrant-operations-management@mail.nasa.gov and publishes a SciENcv quick reference guide [1946](#cite:1946) [1947](#cite:1947).
who_it_is_for: Researchers preparing biographical sketches and [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support) forms [1943](#cite:1943).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1943](#cite:1943).

name: iEdison help desk (NIST)
what: The [iEdison](#term:iedison) help desk is reached at https://contact.iedison.gov [1951](#cite:1951).
who_it_is_for: Recipients reporting inventions under federal funding agreements [1951](#cite:1951).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [1951](#cite:1951).

name: NIH 'New to NIH' registration pages
what: Two [NIH](#term:nih) pages set out, in order, what an organisation registers for and what accounts each person needs, with the time NIH says to allow for each [1909](#cite:1909) [1910](#cite:1910).
who_it_is_for: Organisations and investigators that have not applied to NIH before [1909](#cite:1909).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages read [1909](#cite:1909).

name: OJP Grant Application Resource Guide
what: [OJP](#term:office-of-justice-programs)'s standing guide to its application steps, the two deadlines, the documents required and the late-submission rule, updated September 3, 2026 [619](#cite:619).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to the Office of Justice Programs [619](#cite:619).
cost: No charge is stated on the page read [619](#cite:619).

name: Grants.gov Learn Grants pages
what: [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov)'s learning section explains federal [grants](#term:grant) from the beginning: Grants 101, grant policies, eligibility, terminology, grant-making agencies, systems, reporting and fraud [2074](#cite:2074). Its eligibility page lists the applicant categories used in every notice, including the two non-profit categories [2064](#cite:2064).
who_it_is_for: Current and prospective members of the federal grant community [2074](#cite:2074).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2074](#cite:2074).

name: Grants.gov applicant training videos and user guide
what: Three video series (Introduction to [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), Learning Workspace for Organization Applicants, Quick Clicks), a Workspace overview and an online user guide covering registration, search and application [2075](#cite:2075). Questions go to support@grants.gov; [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration questions go to the Federal Service Desk at fsd.gov [2075](#cite:2075).
who_it_is_for: Organisations and individuals applying through Grants.gov [2075](#cite:2075).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2075](#cite:2075).

name: NIH Grants Process pages
what: [NIH](#term:nih)'s step-by-step account of its [grants](#term:grant) process in six parts: Plan to Apply, Write Application, Submit, Review, Award, and Post-Award Monitoring and Reporting, with links to events and videos [118](#cite:118).
who_it_is_for: People new to NIH funding [118](#cite:118).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [118](#cite:118).

name: HRSA Apply for a Grant pages
what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s applicant pages on completing mandatory registrations, determining eligibility, preparing an application and understanding the [grants](#term:grant) process, with [SF-424](#term:sf-424) application guides and tips [1146](#cite:1146).
who_it_is_for: Organisations applying to HRSA [1146](#cite:1146).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [1146](#cite:1146).

name: NSF information for prospective new awardees
what: [NSF](#term:nsf)'s page and guide (NSF 20-032) for an organisation that has not held an NSF award: what financial documents NSF asks for and how it judges financial viability [2072](#cite:2072).
who_it_is_for: Organisations in line for a first NSF award [2072](#cite:2072).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2072](#cite:2072).

name: IRS Stay Exempt education pages
what: The IRS's training for tax-exempt organisations in four sections: starting out, existing organisations, in-depth topics and a resource library; the old stayexempt.irs.gov address redirects to it [2067](#cite:2067).
who_it_is_for: Leaders, board members and volunteers of non-profits and other tax-exempt entities [2067](#cite:2067).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2067](#cite:2067).

name: IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search (TEOS)
what: The IRS look-up for an organisation's eligibility to receive tax-deductible contributions, its Form 990-series returns and e-Postcards, its [determination letter](#term:determination-letter), and the [Automatic Revocation List](#term:automatic-revocation); it is where a funder checks a non-profit [2059](#cite:2059). The IRS warns of delays in the tool's data [2059](#cite:2059).
who_it_is_for: Funders, donors and the organisations themselves [2059](#cite:2059).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2059](#cite:2059).

name: IRS affirmation letter
what: A letter from the IRS confirming an organisation's tax-exempt status or reflecting a change of name or address, requested from Customer Account Services by phone, letter or fax with the organisation's name, [EIN](#term:ein) and an officer's signature [2066](#cite:2066).
who_it_is_for: Tax-exempt organisations asked for proof of status [2066](#cite:2066).
cost: The page states no cost [2066](#cite:2066).

name: Directory of state charity offices (National Association of State Charity Officials)
what: A directory of the charity regulator in each state, the District of Columbia and the territories, with addresses, telephone numbers and email contacts; the IRS points organisations to it for state [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) registration [2063](#cite:2063) [2062](#cite:2062).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits that solicit contributions [2062](#cite:2062).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2063](#cite:2063).

name: OHRP online human research protection training
what: OHRP's online training, mini-tutorials, videos and webinars on the [HHS](#term:hhs) [human subjects](#term:human-subjects) regulations; [NIH](#term:nih) names OHRP's Human Research Protection Training as one way to meet its education requirement [2076](#cite:2076) [1991](#cite:1991).
who_it_is_for: IRB members and administrators, investigators, institutional officials and others [2076](#cite:2076).
cost: The materials are for public use and may be used and shared freely [2076](#cite:2076).

name: OHRP database of registered IRBs and approved FWAs
what: A public search of registered institutions, IRBs and Federalwide Assurances, and a status page for submissions [1989](#cite:1989) [1985](#cite:1985).
who_it_is_for: Institutions checking their own or a partner's registration or assurance [1989](#cite:1989).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [1989](#cite:1989).

name: OLAW sample Assurance documents and assured-institution look-up
what: OLAW publishes sample [Animal Welfare Assurance](#term:animal-welfare-assurance) documents in PDF and Word and a look-up tool for institutions that hold an Assurance [1996](#cite:1996) [1995](#cite:1995).
who_it_is_for: Institutions that OLAW has asked for an Assurance, and their collaborators [1995](#cite:1995).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages [1996](#cite:1996).

name: ORI sample misconduct policy and assurance contact
what: ORI publishes a sample policy and procedures document for addressing allegations of research misconduct, titled for 2025, and guidance documents for the revised 42 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 93 [2011](#cite:2011). Its assurance staff are at ORI_Assurance@hhs.gov and (240) 453-8400 [2010](#cite:2010).
who_it_is_for: Institutions setting up or revising a research misconduct policy [2011](#cite:2011).
cost: No charge is stated on the pages [2011](#cite:2011).

name: NIH FCOI Policy Development Checklist
what: A checklist [NIH](#term:nih) offers to an institution developing, revising or reviewing its financial conflict of interest policy, updated 06/29/2026 [2003](#cite:2003).
who_it_is_for: Institutions applying for PHS research funding [2003](#cite:2003).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2003](#cite:2003).

name: SECURE Center research security training module
what: A one-hour training module that condenses the four one-hour modules developed by federal agencies; it can be taken online for a certificate of completion or downloaded by an institution for its own learning system [2085](#cite:2085). [NSF](#term:nsf), [NIH](#term:nih) and NASA name it as acceptable [research security training](#term:research-security) [2014](#cite:2014) [33](#cite:33) [383](#cite:383).
who_it_is_for: Senior/key personnel on federal research applications [33](#cite:33).
cost: The page states no cost [2085](#cite:2085).

name: Federal offices that negotiate indirect cost rates
what: [HHS](#term:hhs) Cost Allocation Services negotiates rates with colleges and universities, non-profit organisations, hospitals and state and local governments where HHS is the [cognizant agency](#term:cognizant-agency), taking proposals through its ICAS portal [1860](#cite:1860). The Interior Business Center's [Indirect Cost](#term:indirect-costs) Services negotiates for Interior and as a shared service for other cognizant agencies, with state and local governments, Tribes and non-profits [2073](#cite:2073). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s Cost Analysis and Pre-Award Branch negotiates for the organisations for which NSF is cognizant [163](#cite:163). Read again on 2026-10-04, the Interior Business Center page names no client agency other than Interior, links separate proposal instructions for non-profit organisations, Tribal governments and state and local governments, lists telephone contacts for its office chief (916-930-3828) and two branch chiefs, and states no deadline or review time [2073](#cite:2073).
who_it_is_for: Organisations seeking a [negotiated indirect cost rate](#term:nicra) [1860](#cite:1860).
cost: Neither the HHS page nor the Interior page states a fee for a rate negotiation [1860](#cite:1860) [2073](#cite:2073).

name: Candid Community Partners (public-library access to foundation directories)
what: Secondary source: Candid partners with libraries, [community foundations](#term:community-foundation) and other non-profit resource centres, where the public has free access to Candid's resources; a locator lists the sites [2077](#cite:2077).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits and individuals looking for foundation funders [2077](#cite:2077).
cost: Free to users at partner locations; the partner organisation pays Candid from $2,995 a year [2077](#cite:2077).

name: National Council of Nonprofits and state associations of non-profits
what: Secondary source: a national network of state non-profit associations that publishes guidance under "Running a Nonprofit" and "Trends and Policy Issues", a free newsletter, and a finder for the association in each state [2078](#cite:2078).
who_it_is_for: Charitable non-profits [2078](#cite:2078).
cost: The newsletter is described as free; no charge is stated for the guidance pages [2078](#cite:2078).

name: COGR (association of research institutions)
what: Secondary source: an association of more than 230 research institutions that publishes comment letters, monthly updates and issue briefs on federal research policy and regulation, arranged by topic [2079](#cite:2079).
who_it_is_for: Research offices at universities and research institutes [2079](#cite:2079).
cost: Membership is institutional; the page does not say which publications are open to non-members [2079](#cite:2079).

name: NCURA (National Council of University Research Administrators)
what: Secondary source: the professional association for research administrators; its open resources include a YouTube channel and the journal Research Management Review, while tutorials, webinars, podcasts and the magazine are for members [2080](#cite:2080).
who_it_is_for: Research administrators [2080](#cite:2080).
cost: Some resources are open and others are for members [2080](#cite:2080).

name: The institution's limited-submission (internal competition) process
what: Where a foundation takes only one or a few nominees from an institution, the institution runs its own internal competition first. One university's notice for the 2027 Pew Scholars states that it "is allowed to submit one [nomination](#term:institutional-nomination)" and sets an internal process to choose the nominee [2175](#cite:2175). For the Keck Research Program the contact is the central development office, which knows the designated liaison [2134](#cite:2134).
who_it_is_for: Faculty at an institution that may nominate to a limited programme [2175](#cite:2175).
cost: Not stated on the pages read [2175](#cite:2175).

name: The Kresge Foundation contact form
what: The route Kresge gives for an organisation to introduce itself; the foundation aims to respond within three business days [2348](#cite:2348).
who_it_is_for: Organisations not yet funded by Kresge [2348](#cite:2348).
cost: No charge is stated [2348](#cite:2348).

name: Robert W. Woodruff Foundation informal inquiry
what: The foundation asks a prospective applicant to email an informal inquiry to fdns@woodruff.org to learn whether to apply [2313](#cite:2313).
who_it_is_for: Organisations located or operating in Georgia [2313](#cite:2313).
cost: No charge is stated [2313](#cite:2313).

name: RWJF programme officer contacts on each funding opportunity
what: Each Robert Wood Johnson Foundation funding opportunity page names a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) contact [2271](#cite:2271).
who_it_is_for: Applicants to an RWJF call [2271](#cite:2271).
cost: No charge is stated [2271](#cite:2271).

name: Ford Foundation idea submission form
what: A short online form through which anyone may send the Ford Foundation an idea; it is not a [grant](#term:grant) proposal, which Ford does not accept [unsolicited](#term:unsolicited-request) [2259](#cite:2259).
who_it_is_for: Organisations and people with no existing tie to Ford [2259](#cite:2259).
cost: No charge is stated [2259](#cite:2259).

name: Where to read a foundation's tax filing free
what: Three free sources hold [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) and [Form 990](#term:form-990) filings [2059](#cite:2059) [2398](#cite:2398) [2399](#cite:2399). The IRS [Tax Exempt Organization Search](#term:tax-exempt-organization-search) covers Form 990 series returns, Pub. 78 data, Form 990-N, the [automatic revocation list](#term:automatic-revocation) and [determination letters](#term:determination-letter) [2059](#cite:2059). ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer holds Form 990, 990-EZ and 990-PF filings going back as far as 2001 and refers to over 1.8 million filings [2398](#cite:2398). Candid search is free to anyone who registers, with limited search results and basic profile views on the free plan [2402](#cite:2402) [2399](#cite:2399). A foundation must also provide its own return on request for three years, and some post it on their websites [2461](#cite:2461) [2430](#cite:2430).
who_it_is_for: Anyone checking what a foundation has funded, how large it is, and whether its Form 990-PF says it accepts [unsolicited requests](#term:unsolicited-request) [2387](#cite:2387).
cost: The IRS and ProPublica tools carry no charge on the pages read [2059](#cite:2059) [2398](#cite:2398). Candid's free plan is $0 and its paid plans start at $219 a month [2399](#cite:2399).

name: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer
what: A database of non-profit tax filings built from the data the IRS releases [2398](#cite:2398). It includes [Form 990](#term:form-990), Form 990EZ and Form 990PF filings, going back as far as 2001, and refers to over 1.8 million filings [2398](#cite:2398). Each organisation has a page reached by its [employer identification number](#term:ein); the page for Silicon Valley [Community Foundation](#term:community-foundation) gave its assets, revenue and expenses for the year ending December 2024 [2415](#cite:2415). An API is documented [2398](#cite:2398).
who_it_is_for: Anyone who wants to read a foundation's [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) or a [public charity](#term:public-charity)'s Form 990 without an account [2398](#cite:2398).
cost: No payment is asked for on the pages read [2398](#cite:2398).

name: Candid search (free plan and paid directory)
what: Candid search is the product that now holds Candid's funder directory; it "combines decades of trusted data from both Foundation Directory and GuideStar" and claims 304k+ funder profiles and 29M+ [grants](#term:grant) [2400](#cite:2400). Candid launched it on January 15, 2026 and says it is free for anyone who registers at candid.org [2402](#cite:2402). The free plan gives limited search results and basic profile views; unlimited results, full profiles and grants data need a paid plan [2399](#cite:2399). The address that used to list [requests for proposals](#term:open-call), philanthropynewsdigest.org/rfps, now redirects to a Candid search page where requests for proposals are a feature of the subscription plans [2401](#cite:2401).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits and others researching funders [2402](#cite:2402). Small non-profits with under $1 million in revenue receive complimentary Premium access upon earning a Gold Seal of Transparency [2402](#cite:2402). Free access is also offered at Candid partner locations [2403](#cite:2403).
cost: Free plan $0; Premium monthly $219/month; Premium annual $1,199/year and Ultimate annual $1,699/year on the pricing page [2399](#cite:2399); the product page returned $2,199/year and $2,499/year for the same two plans [2400](#cite:2400). Enterprise is custom-priced [2399](#cite:2399).

name: Candid near you (partner locations with free access)
what: Candid's locator page says "Partner locations throughout the U.S. and internationally offer access to Candid and nonprofit fundraising resources for free" and offers a map to find the nearest one [2403](#cite:2403). The page as fetched does not say what kinds of institution the partners are, how many there are, or which Candid product they give access to [2403](#cite:2403).
who_it_is_for: Anyone who wants to use Candid's directory without paying for a subscription [2403](#cite:2403).
cost: Free at the partner location, as the page states [2403](#cite:2403).

name: IRS Form 990 series downloads (bulk e-file data)
what: The IRS page that offers "all the most recent 990 Series filings on record in XML formats", by year and month, with a CSV index for each year; on 2026-10-04 it listed 2019 through 2026 [2397](#cite:2397).
who_it_is_for: People who can work with XML files and want many returns at once; a single return is easier to read through the [Tax Exempt Organization Search](#term:tax-exempt-organization-search) or Nonprofit Explorer [2397](#cite:2397) [2059](#cite:2059) [2398](#cite:2398).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2397](#cite:2397).

name: Community Foundation Locator (Council on Foundations)
what: A map-based locator of [community foundations](#term:community-foundation), searchable by state, with a filter that shows only foundations accredited under the Community Foundations National Standards [2404](#cite:2404). The Council says more than 900 community foundations operate across every state and that over 500 have earned the National Standards Seal [2405](#cite:2405).
who_it_is_for: A non-profit or researcher looking for the community foundation that serves its area [2404](#cite:2404).
cost: No charge is stated on the page [2404](#cite:2404).

name: Regional associations of grantmakers (United Philanthropy Forum member directory)
what: United Philanthropy Forum's member directory lists its "nearly 100 members", which are regional and national philanthropy-serving organisations, and can be filtered by organisation type and region [2406](#cite:2406). Arizona Grantmakers Forum is one member listed [2406](#cite:2406). Some regional associations publish a common [grant](#term:grant) application form: Philanthropy Missouri publishes the Missouri Common Grant Application [2459](#cite:2459).
who_it_is_for: Grant seekers who want to find the body that convenes funders in their region and any shared forms or directories it publishes [2406](#cite:2406).
cost: The directory page states no charge [2406](#cite:2406).

name: Find Your State Association of Nonprofits (National Council of Nonprofits)
what: A map and directory of state associations of non-profits; a state coloured grey has no member organisation in the network at present [2407](#cite:2407).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits looking for the association in their state [2407](#cite:2407).
cost: The locator page states no charge; each state association sets its own membership terms, which the page read does not give [2407](#cite:2407).

name: Common grant application forms
what: A common [grant](#term:grant) application "allows grantmakers and grantseekers to work from a common set of questions and definitions", in the words of the Missouri form's publisher [2459](#cite:2459). Two were found still published [2459](#cite:2459) [2460](#cite:2460). The Missouri Common Grant Application, Version 2.0, updated in 2017, comes as a full application, a short form usable as a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent), budget templates, a user guide and a funder guide [2459](#cite:2459). The Colorado Common Grant Application is offered in Word format with a separate form for capital campaigns and a user's guide [2460](#cite:2460). Neither page says how many funders accept the form [2459](#cite:2459) [2460](#cite:2460).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits applying to funders in a region where a common form is in use; each funder's own guidelines say whether it accepts the form [2459](#cite:2459).
cost: Both are free to download [2459](#cite:2459) [2460](#cite:2460).

name: Find Your United Way
what: United Way Worldwide's locator for local United Ways, by country and state or by zip code; it counts 1,100+ United Ways in more than 30 countries and territories [2456](#cite:2456). United Way Worldwide says "Most program funding happens locally, so we encourage you to reach out to your local United Way to learn more" [2457](#cite:2457).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits that deliver local services and want to know how their local United Way funds programmes [2457](#cite:2457).
cost: No charge is stated [2456](#cite:2456).

name: Giving circle directory (Philanthropy Together)
what: Philanthropy Together, a network for giving circles, links a directory of circles from its home page [2458](#cite:2458). The count of circles did not render through the fetch layer [2458](#cite:2458).
who_it_is_for: Non-profits and donors looking for a giving circle in their area or field [2458](#cite:2458).
cost: No charge is stated [2458](#cite:2458).

name: GivingTuesday 990 Data Lake and data marts
what: GivingTuesday's 990 Data Infrastructure project keeps a copy of electronically filed [Form 990](#term:form-990), 990-EZ and [990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) returns, which it calls the 990 Data Lake, and publishes tables cut from them, which it calls data marts [2473](#cite:2473) [2474](#cite:2474). For [private foundations](#term:private-foundation) the marts include a table of basic fields with one row for each return, a table with one row for each [grant](#term:grant) paid during the year, and a table with one row for each grant approved for future payment [2477](#cite:2477) [2475](#cite:2475) [2476](#cite:2476). A data dictionary lists every column against the form part and line it comes from [2474](#cite:2474). The raw XML returns are in the Amazon S3 bucket "gt990datalake-rawdata" under "EfileData/XmlFiles" [2478](#cite:2478).
who_it_is_for: Researchers, practitioners and developers, in the project's words "a one-stop resource for researchers, social sector practitioners, and developers" [2473](#cite:2473). A grant seeker reading one foundation is served by the filing hosts already in the pack; this source suits a site or an analyst that reads many returns at once [2474](#cite:2474).
cost: The access page says a free Amazon Web Services account is required and that users "will not be charged for using the Data Lake" [2478](#cite:2478). The data use licence page names the Open Database License 1.0 and the Database Contents License 1.0 [2479](#cite:2479).
limits: The home page and access page do not say which filing years are held or how soon a return appears [2473](#cite:2473) [2478](#cite:2478). On 2026-10-04 the address for Lilly Endowment's return for 2025, which another filing host lists, returned HTTP 404, while its return for 2024 loaded [2511](#cite:2511). The grants-paid table for Form 990-PF has no column for the recipient's [EIN](#term:ein); the table for Form 990 Schedule I has one [2475](#cite:2475) [2508](#cite:2508).
